Message.Name: Send Key Message
Message.Description: Sent by MMDH to the client on TCP session establishment. Carries Diffie-Hellman parameters (Prime, Generator, PrimeOrderSubgroup) and the OMD Public Key concatenated with a 16-byte Initialization Vector for AES-CFB password encryption during Logon.

Field.Name: Prime
Field.Description: A large Prime number in hexadecimal format.

Field.Name: Generator
Field.Description: Generator — a primitive root modulo the value of Prime in hexadecimal format.

Field.Name: PrimeOrderSubgroup
Field.Description: Prime-order subgroup value used by the Diffie-Hellman exchange.

Field.Name: OMDPublicKey
Field.Description: First 128 bytes: the Public Key being shared. Last 16 bytes: the Initialization Vector for AES-CFB.

Message.Name: Logon Message
Message.Description: Client-to-server message initiating authentication. Password is encrypted using an AES key derived from the Diffie-Hellman shared secret (SHA-256 hashed) with the IV received in SendKey. InternalSeqNum is 0 at start of day or the last received internal sequence number for intraday recovery. If EncryptedNewPasswordLen/EncryptedNewPassword are populated, the logon is treated as a password-change attempt.

Field.Name: Username
Field.Description: Username to log on, padded with binary null characters.

Field.Name: InternalSeqNum
Field.Description: Set to the last received internal sequence number for intraday recovery, or 0 at start of day.

Field.Name: ClientPublicKey
Field.Description: Client public key generated per Diffie-Hellman exchange.

Field.Name: EncryptedPasswordLen
Field.Description: Length of the EncryptedPassword in bytes.

Field.Name: EncryptedNewPasswordLen
Field.Description: Length of the EncryptedNewPassword in bytes.

Field.Name: EncryptedNewPassword
Field.Description: AES-CFB encrypted new password (for password change; empty for normal logon).

Message.Name: Logon Response Message
Message.Description: Server response to a Logon request. Carries HeartBtInterval (heartbeat interval the client must honour), SessionStatus, and PasswordExpiryDays. A TCP disconnect follows SessionStatus 5, 6, 104 or 105 — client should reconnect and wait for a new SendKey before re-attempting Logon.

Field.Name: HeartBtInterval
Field.Description: Heartbeat interval (seconds) the client and server must honour to keep the session alive.

Field.Name: PasswordExpiryDays
Field.Description: Number of days left before password expires.

Message.Name: Logout Message
Message.Description: Server-initiated message informing the client they have been logged out. The server follows with a TCP disconnect.

Value.Name: New Session Password Does Not Comply With Policy
